Your agent can be fooled. The scope can't.

Nitaq installs between your AI agent and its tools. An order hidden in an e-mail, a page or a skill file — in Egyptian Arabic, Arabizi or Base64 — that tries to send your data out or read your keys is refused: it is outside the scope.

Download the Nitaq app — no terminal needed

Everything on this site, in one app on your computer: your agents, skills, the Gateway and the Nitaq agent with approve and deny buttons. It runs on your computer only.

  • Windows 10 and 11Nitaq-Setup-Windows-x64.exeDownload the installer and double-click it: it adds Nitaq to the Start menu and the desktop, with an uninstaller. If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway (the app is not code-signed yet). or portable .exeDownloadyour computer
  • macOS (Apple Silicon)Nitaq-macOS.dmgOpen the DMG and drag Nitaq into Applications. The first time, right-click it and choose Open. or .zipDownloadyour computer

The agent needs a free Gemini key, which you paste into the app once and never leaves your computer. Developers can install it with pipx, below. All releases and notes

The agent can be fooled. Nitaq can't.

nitaq agent is a light terminal agent like Codex, running on Gemini. Everything it reads is scanned, and every command it wants to run is judged before it happens. We tried it with two booby-trapped skill files — below is a real recording of an actual run.

skill1.md

An injected order in Franco: found and removed

A strong article-writing skill with one paragraph that tells the AI to collect your data and photos and POST them to an outside server. Nitaq cut it out before the model saw it, and the model told you what happened.

An innocent-looking command: stopped, permissions reduced

A skill for an HTML page about a book. Its text passed the scan with a warning; the model was fooled and tried to run curl uploading the .env file. Nitaq stopped the command before it ran and reduced the agent's permissions until you approve.

Connect your AI to Nitaq — from here

Run Nitaq Gateway on your computer and this page talks to it straight from your browser: see the tools it guards, the protection state, and scan text through it. Then connect it to Claude or Gemini.

  1. Start the Gateway and allow this site

    $ nitaq gateway --allow-origin https://SITE

    Open the site from its own domain so the command shows the right address.

  2. This page talks only to the URL you pasted, straight from your browser. Nothing goes to the site's server, and the URL is not stored.

  3. Connect it to your AI

    claude.ai: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector

    claude.ai needs an https URL, so run this tunnel and use the address it prints in place of the local one.

    $ cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8787
    https://<tunnel>/mcp/<secret>

    Claude Code

    $ claude mcp add --transport http nitaq http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp/<secret>

    Gemini CLI (~/.gemini/settings.json)

    {"mcpServers": {"nitaq": {"httpUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp/<secret>"}}}

The same protection for AI in the cloud

nitaq gateway is an MCP server you run on your computer; connect Claude or any cloud AI through it to your e-mail and files. E-mails are scanned before the AI sees them, and anything sent outside waits for your approval on this dashboard.

Protection covers the tools that pass through the Gateway only. The mailbox in the picture is a demo; no e-mail leaves the computer.

It stands between the agent and its tools — and decides from the action, not the words

It doesn't try to understand which language the text is in. It looks at the request: where is this tool sending data? which file is it reading? That is why Egyptian, Arabizi or Base64 make no difference to it.

The danger is complete when three things meet

  • Private datayour files, keys, mail
  • Outside contenta page, an e-mail, a skill, a tool description
  • A way to send oute-mail, web request, curl

Nitaq shuts the two legs where the damage happens: reading secret files, and sending to anywhere not allowed. This framing is the “lethal trifecta” (Simon Willison, June 2025). simonwillison.net

AgentClaude Code · Gemini CLI · Gemini agent Nitaqproxy · hook · gateway · policy Tools & internetMCP · Bash · fetch · Read · mail
nitaq mcp-proxyMCP proxy
Every local MCP server runs behind Nitaq: denied calls return an error, and tools whose description contains an injection are hidden from the agent.
nitaq hook claude-codeClaude Code guard
A hook before every tool answers with the documented deny format; a hook after it records hosts that appeared in outside content.
~/.nitaq/policy.jsonA clear policy
Strict: any host not on the list is blocked. Smart (taint): only hosts seen in outside content are blocked. Secret files may not be read.
nitaq discoverDiscover and scan
Finds agent configs, skills and MCP servers on your machine and scans them — read-only, nothing is changed.

When an agent reads an e-mail, a page or a skill file, any sentence inside can be taken as an order. This is indirect prompt injection, and OWASP ranks prompt injection first in its 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications. OWASP LLM01

Not supported directly (yet): Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code / Copilot, Codex CLI, Windsurf. Any cloud AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini…) can reach your e-mail and files through nitaq gateway (MCP); Nitaq guards the tools that pass through it — not the tools built into the provider's own service.

What Nitaq does not do

Nitaq reduces the damage an injected instruction can cause; it does not stop a model from following it.

  • It does not prevent “jailbreaks”, and it does not stop the model from being fooled.
  • Tampering inside what is allowed (a false statement in a normal reply, data sent to an allowed host) is not stopped.
  • Remote (HTTP/SSE) MCP servers cannot be wrapped by a local proxy.
  • The Claude Code guard follows the docs but has not been exercised in a real session with a model.
  • Hosts the model assembles from pieces at run time can slip through.
All limits in detail

Built to answer a question

Do injection filters weaken when the attack is written in Egyptian Arabic, MSA or Arabizi, or encoded? Does a guard that never reads the text hold? The Nitaq benchmark measures this in a fully mock environment, with a frozen scanner, and every number comes from results files.

Results and conclusions are written by the student who owns the project, not by AI.

Report and method

Before you install

Does it work with ChatGPT or Gemini on the web?

No. Those run on the providers' servers. What you can do: check a file before you hand it over, with the phone checker.

Does it send any data out?

No. Nitaq itself makes no network connection. The local log holds the tool name, the rule and the hosts — never the content.

Will it change my settings by itself?

No. Installing changes nothing. Protection happens only when you run protect --apply and type APPLY, after a backup.

Why doesn't the language matter to it?

Because the decision is made from the request itself (the host, the file), not from the words that fooled the model.

Will strict mode block legitimate things?

Yes, that is its cost: any site not on the list is blocked. If that is too much, smart mode (taint) blocks only hosts seen in outside content.

Is it free?

Yes, open source under the MIT licence.

Set the scope before someone tries.

A read-only discovery first, then you decide.

$ pipx install "git+https://github.com/fernata-dev/Nitaq.git"
